content:
We need retrosynthesis route up to 3 steps, leaves commercially available, total price <=9999. Need to propose route and output JSON.

We need to find suitable disconnections. Target: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Structure: a tolyl sulfonamide attached to a phenyl ring bearing a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (anilide). So overall: p-tolyl-sulfonyl-phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-phenyl-NH2? Actually the amide attaches to an aniline (Nc3ccccc3N) meaning the amide nitrogen attached to phenyl with an NH2 para? Wait: C(=O)N c3ccccc3N: amide nitrogen attached to phenyl that also has an NH2 substituent (aniline). So product is a sulfonamide linking two phenyls, plus a cinnamamide with an aniline.

Potential retrosynthesis: disconnection at sulfonamide formation (sulfonyl chloride + aniline). Also disconnection at amide formation (acid chloride + aniline). Also disconnection at the double bond (Heck coupling or Wittig). Simpler: use commercially available sulfonyl chloride (p-toluenesulfonyl chloride) and aniline derivative (the phenyl-sulfonyl phenyl with the cinnamoyl anilide). But that seems complex.

Better: break at sulfonamide: target = aryl-sulfonyl-aryl. So we can get sulfonyl chloride (p-toluenesulfonyl chloride) and the aryl amine (the other phenyl with the cinnamoyl anilide). That aryl amine could be synthesized via amide formation between cinnamic acid derivative and aniline (with NH2). So route:

Step 1: Form sulfonamide: p-toluenesulfonyl chloride + aryl amine (compound A) -> target.

Step 2: Synthesize aryl amine A: start from 4-aminophenyl (or 4-aminobenzaldehyde?) Actually A is phenyl bearing sulfonyl group (attached) and also the cinnamoyl anilide attached at para? Wait the target: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the sulfonamide nitrogen attached to phenyl ring (c2ccc...). That phenyl also has the cinnamoyl anilide substituent at para? The SMILES: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. The sulfonamide nitrogen attached to the phenyl (c2). The phenyl has a substituent /C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N at para position relative to sulfonamide? The SMILES shows c2ccc( ... )cc2, with the substituent at position 4 relative to the sulfonamide. So the aryl amine (the phenyl) is not an amine; it's a phenyl with a side chain containing an amide attached to an aniline. The sulfonamide nitrogen attaches to the phenyl (as sulfonamide). So the aryl amine needed for sulfonamide formation is the phenyl with the side chain (which contains an aniline). That phenyl is not an amine; it's a phenyl with a side chain that includes an aniline (NH2). So we need to have that phenyl with a free amine (the aniline) to react with sulfonyl chloride? Wait sulfonamide formation uses an amine (nucleophile) reacting with sulfonyl chloride. In target, the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the tolyl group (p-tolyl) and to the phenyl ring (c2...). So the nitrogen is bridging between tolyl sulfonyl and phenyl. So the nitrogen originates from an amine that is attached to the phenyl (the phenyl is the amine). So the phenyl must have an NH group (aniline) that is sulfonylated. Indeed the phenyl has an NH (attached to sulfonyl) and also a side chain with amide to another aniline. So the phenyl is a 4-(cinnamoyl-anilide) aniline (i.e., 4-aminophenyl with side chain). So we can start from 4-aminophenyl (p-aminophenyl) and then attach the side chain (cinnamoyl-anilide) via amide formation? Actually the side chain is attached via a carbon-carbon double bond to the phenyl (para). That's a styryl group attached to the phenyl. So we need to install a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide onto the phenyl at para position. That could be done via Heck coupling of 4-iodo-aniline with an acrylamide, or via Wittig/condensation.

Simplify: Use commercially available 4-aminobenzaldehyde (or 4-aminobenzyl) to do Knoevenagel condensation with an appropriate amide? Actually we need C=C-C(=O)-NH-Ph-NH2. Could be formed by condensation of 4-aminobenzaldehyde with an amide? Not straightforward.

Alternative: break at amide: use cinnamic acid (commercial) and aniline (commercial) to form amide (via coupling reagents). Then attach that amide to phenyl via a Heck coupling of 4-iodoaniline with the cinnamic acid derivative? Actually the amide is attached to the phenyl via the double bond: phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2. So the phenyl side chain is a trans-cinnamoyl anilide attached via the double bond to phenyl. So we could start from 4-iodoaniline (commercial) and do a Heck coupling with trans-cinnamoyl aniline (i.e., trans-cinnamoyl aniline). But trans-cinnamoyl aniline is an anilide of cinnamic acid (i.e., C6H5-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2). That itself could be made from cinnamic acid + aniline.

Thus route:

Step 1: Synthesize trans-cinnamoyl aniline (compound B): Cinnamic acid + aniline (via amide coupling). Both are cheap.

Step 2: Perform Heck coupling between 4-iodoaniline (commercial) and compound B (as the alkene partner) to give the phenyl with side chain (compound A) i.e., 4-(cinnamoyl-anilide)aniline.

Step 3: Sulfonamide formation: react compound A (the aniline) with p-toluenesulfonyl chloride to give target.

All leaves: p-toluenesulfonyl chloride, 4-iodoaniline, cinnamic acid, aniline (for amide). All commercially available and cheap.

We need to verify templates for amide formation (acid + amine) and Heck coupling (aryl halide + alkene). Also sulfonamide formation (aryl amine + sulfonyl chloride). Use search to find templates.

Let's search for amide formation template (functional_groups_formed: amides).
